analysis.title: US Watch: Oct jobs: A clean sweep for the hawks
key_insights: The October jobs report was hawkish across the board. NFP rose 165k (private 159k), well above expectations, with 84k of upward revisions to the prior two months. The three-month average is 137k, substantially above breakeven.

The unemployment rate was nearly unchanged on an unrounded basis (4.175% to 4.141%), shown as 4.1%. This came despite a one-tenth rise in the participation rate to 61.9%, the third straight increase. Household employment rose 463k for a third strong month, and unemployment fell 41k.
BofA says the report should ease some jitters and clear the way for a December hike. Inflation is still described as more important than the labor data.

Private payroll strength was led by service-producing jobs (+144k). Professional and business services added 70k, education and health 53k (mostly healthcare), and trade, transportation and utilities 22k. The trade sector is likely supported by elevated imports from AI capex and front-loading amid tariff and war uncertainty. Leisure and hospitality lost 13k jobs.
Goods-producing jobs rose 15k, with manufacturing +19k on the AI boom and some broadening beyond it. Construction unexpectedly lost 3k jobs after a period of strength from data center buildout.

Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% m/m, above expectations, and September was revised up to 0.3%. Year-over-year wage growth is 3.1%, still below headline inflation, but the 3-month annualized pace rebounded from 2.9% to 3.9%. Aggregate weekly payroll growth firmed a tenth to 4.5% y/y.
The U6 underemployment rate rose from 7.6% to 7.9% alongside longer unemployment duration, but BofA says the Fed has not focused on these measures lately.
BofA says the strong report keeps the Fed focused on inflation and on track to hike again in December. It says the policy put for stocks should be struck considerably lower after this data.

US rates rose up to 7bps at the front end after the release, with about half of the move in real rates. The market now prices 20bps for December (80% probability). The 1-year-forward Fed path rose 6-8bps, implying a terminal rate of 4.35%. BofA keeps its bias to be paid front end and for flatter curves.

The USD rose about 0.25% against most G10 currencies after the release, a restrained move relative to the size of the beat. AUD and JPY were little changed. BofA expects the USD can keep trading higher on resilient US growth and sticky core inflation.

The Canadian dollar underperformed after Canada's October employment report showed a third straight monthly drop in employment. The Canadian unemployment rate rose to 6.7% from a yearly low of 6.4% in August.
